Market and state attitudes in Ukraine

A synthesis of attitudes toward markets and the state’s role in the economy, drawn from international and Ukrainian surveys.

Sources and methodology

95 question-level trends. Each series has at least two observations and a latest observation in 2019 or later. Lines connect actual survey years.

Numeric questions show weighted means with 95% confidence intervals. Ordered responses combine positive and negative categories, retaining middle and missing responses. Nominal questions show all options. Numeric means use valid answers; categorical shares include nonresponse.

  • WVS: Adults aged 18+, national weights, aligned scale directions and approximate intervals. Haerpfer et al. (2024), time series v5.0.
  • EVS: Weighted adult estimates and approximate intervals; shown separately from WVS for comparison. EVS (2022), ZA7503 v3.0.0.
  • Pew: Published Ukrainian percentages, retaining rounding and nonresponse. Fieldwork years are used, including 2015 for the report published in 2017. Reports and toplines.
  • Monitoring: Published national tables; differently worded questions remain separate. No intervals are inferred from percentages alone. Institute of Sociology, NAS of Ukraine.
  • ESS: Weighted adult estimates; 2022/2024 intervals account for strata and sampling clusters, earlier intervals are approximate. The 2022 observation is a separate Ukrainian ESS-related study. The 2006–07 fieldwork point is plotted at 2007. Dataset editions and citations.
  • ISSP: Weighted adult estimates for 2009 and 2019, with approximate intervals. Monetary amounts are monthly after-tax UAH at current prices. ISSP 2009; Oksamytna and Ivashchenko, Ukraine 2019.
  • LiTS: Included in the project’s aggregate tables; its 2016 endpoint falls outside this gallery’s selection. EBRD and World Bank, rounds I–III.

Territorial coverage and survey methods change across waves. Comparability details.
